items.title: Association Between Intradialytic Foot Temperature Gradients and Severe Peripheral Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Hemodialysis: Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is prevalent in hemodialysis (HD) patients but remains difficult to diagnose due to unreliable ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements caused by vascular calcification. We hypothesized that monitoring foot temperatures and their changes during HD, provoked by hemodynamic shifts, could serve as a novel diagnostic tool for detecting severe PAD. This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD. In this prospective observational study, we recruited 109 patients undergoing chronic maintenance HD. Skin temperatures were monitored continuously at the instep and sole during HD sessions using wearable sensors (Temp Pal, iWEECARE Co, Ltd), which are wireless, nanochip-based mHealth thermometers with ±0.05 °C accuracy. The diagnostic performance of temperature parameters, specifically the temperature difference between the wrist and foot at the end of HD, was evaluated against vascular duplex ultrasound (DUS). Severe PAD was defined as abnormal (monophasic or absent) flow in the distal posterior tibial artery (PTA) or anterior tibial artery (ATA). Patients with abnormal tibial flow on DUS exhibited significantly different temperature gradients between the wrist and foot at the end of dialysis compared to those with normal flow. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that the wrist-foot temperature difference at the sole effectively discriminated abnormal ATA flow (area under the curve [AUC] 64.5%, 95% CI 57.8%-70.9%) and abnormal PTA flow (AUC 62.0%, 95% CI 55.2%-68.5%). Notably, an instep wrist-foot temperature difference cutoff of -2.2 °C or less yielded a specificity of 97.6% (95% CI 94.0%-99.3%) for detecting abnormal PTA flow. Intradialytic foot temperature monitoring, particularly the temperature gradient between the wrist and foot, significantly correlates with severe tibial artery flow abnormalities. This method offers an accessible, noninvasive screening adjunct to the ABI for detecting severe PAD in the HD population. These findings indicate an association rather than a standalone diagnostic test; given the modest discriminative ability, external validation is warranted.

items.title: Nurses' Attitudes and Experiences With Generative AI in Clinical Practice: Qualitative Systematic Review.
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative AI (GenAI) holds transformative potential for clinical nursing practice, yet its integration also brings significant risks and uncertainties. Despite growing discourse on AI in health care, frontline nurses' firsthand experiences, perceptions, and practical needs regarding GenAI remain largely under-synthesized in the existing literature. This systematic review aimed to synthesize qualitative evidence to clarify the core themes related to clinical nurses' perceptions, experiences, obstacles, and requirements when using GenAI in real-world clinical settings. A systematic search was conducted across 10 electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, VIP Information, SinoMed, and Wanfang) for records published between January 2018 and June 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative and mixed methods studies involving registered nurses that explored their perceptions and experiences of GenAI in clinical practice. Two independent reviewers (MMW and CYZ) performed study selection, quality appraisal, and data extraction, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research. Extracted data encompassed study characteristics, participant demographics, and GenAI-related contextual factors. Data synthesis followed Thomas and Harden's 3-phase thematic synthesis: initial inductive coding generated descriptive themes, which were subsequently integrated with the Technology Acceptance Model for Artificial Intelligence in Nursing (TAM-AIN) framework to develop higher-order analytical themes. Certainty in the evidence was evaluated using the GRADE-CERQual (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation-Confidence in the Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research). Of the 4350 initially identified records, 13 studies from 6 countries (China: n=6; Saudi Arabia: n=3; United States, Singapore, Australia, and South Korea: n=1 each) met the inclusion criteria, encompassing qualitative data from 234 registered nurses. Three main themes emerged: patterns of nurses' engagement with GenAI (ranging from passive observation to proactive integration), multidimensional perceived threats to adoption (functional, professional, and accountability-related), and the moderating role of organizational readiness, which influenced whether these threats hindered or facilitated GenAI uptake in practice. The GRADE-CERQual assessment showed moderate to high confidence in all findings. Nurses' engagement with GenAI ranges from passive observation to proactive integration, accompanied by legitimate concerns about functional reliability, professional role displacement, and accountability ambiguity. The moderating role of organizational readiness further highlights that training, tool optimization, and institutional governance remain critical yet often unmet. These findings necessitate coordinated efforts across workforce development, technological design, and regulatory frameworks. Future research should prioritize the development of clinically validated, context-aware GenAI systems that incorporate human-in-the-loop oversight, ensuring that efficiency gains do not compromise the delivery of compassionate, person-centered care.

items.title: Blood serotonin, ionized magnesium, cardiac troponin I, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide concentrations, and mitral valve billowing in horses with mitral valve regurgitation.
items.abstract: Serotonin, ionized magnesium (iMg), cardiac biomarkers, and mitral valve prolapse are extensively investigated in humans and dogs with mitral valve regurgitation (MR), but not in horses. To investigate serotonin, iMg, cardiac troponin I (cTnI), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations and degree of mitral valve billowing (MVB) in horses with MR. Eighty controls (no/trivial MR), 122 horses with MR (92 mild, 24 moderate, 6 severe). Prospective cross-sectional observational study. All horses underwent echocardiography with MVB distance assessment and MR classification. Platelet-poor plasma serotonin and serum iMg, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were determined. Controls and horses with different MR grades, biomarker concentrations, and MVB distance were compared using (non-)parametric tests. Ionized magnesium concentration was lower in MR compared to controls (mean difference, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; P = .01), but showed no correlation with billowing distance. The billowing distance was higher in horses with MR than in controls (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P < .001; parietal: median difference, 0.3 cm; 95% CI, 0.2-0.3; P < .001), and in horses with a crescendo compared to a holosystolic MR jet (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P = .003; parietal: median difference, 0.1 cm; 95% CI, 0.0-0.2; P = .01). No differences in serotonin, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were detected. Mitral valve billowing is to some extent likely physiological. The association of serotonin and iMg in MVB and MR requires further investigation. Both cTnI and NT-proBNP showed limited use as biomarkers of MR severity. Achtergrondinformatie: Serotonine, geïoniseerd magnesium (iMg), cardiale biomarkers en mitraalklep prolaps werden reeds uitgebreid onderzocht bij mensen en honden met mitraalklep regurgitatie (MR), in tegenstelling tot paarden met MR. Hypothese/Doelstelling: Het onderzoeken van de serotonine, iMg, cardiaal troponine I (cTnI) en N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentraties en de mate van bolling van de mitraalklep naar het linker atrium (MVB) bij paarden met MR. Studiepopulatie: Tachtig controle paarden (geen/triviaal MR), 122 paarden met MR (92 mild, 24 matig, 6 erg). Materiaal en methoden: Prospectieve cross-sectionele observationele studie. Alle paarden ondergingen echocardiografie, waarna de mate van MVB gemeten werd en MR classificatie uitgevoerd werd. De concentraties van serotonine in bloedplaatjesarm plasma en van iMg, cTnI en NT-proBNP in serum werden bepaald. Controle paarden en paarden met verschillende MR graden, biomarker concentraties en de mate van MVB werden onderling vergeleken aan de hand van (non-)parametrische testen. Resultaten: De concentratie iMg was lager bij paarden met MR in vergelijking met controle paarden (gemiddeld verschil, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% BI, 0.01-0.05; P = 0.01), maar vertoonde geen correlatie met de mate van MVB. De mate van MVB was hoger bij paarden met MR dan bij controle paarden (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P < 0.001; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.3 cm; 95% BI, 0.2-0.3; P < 0.001), en bij paarden met een crescendo MR jet in vergelijking met paarden met een holosystolische MR jet (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P = 0.003; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.1 cm; 95% BI, 0.0-0.2; P = 0.01). Er werden geen verschillen gedetecteerd in de concentraties van serotonine, cTnI en NT-proBNP. Conclusies en klinisch belang: De mate van MVB is tot op een bepaalde hoogte waarschijnlijk fysiologisch. De rol van serotonine en iMg in MVB en MR vergt verder onderzoek. Zowel cTnI als NT-proBNP vertoonden een beperkte meerwaarde als biomarkers bij het bepalen van de ernst van MR. This study investigated four biomarkers in the blood of horses with and without mitral valve regurgitation (MR), a condition in which the heart’s mitral valve does not close completely and allows blood to leak backwards. We also examined whether these biomarkers were related to billowing of the mitral valve, where part of the valve bulges backwards during contraction of the heart. The main findings were: Horses with MR had lower blood levels of ionized magnesium (iMg) than horses without MR.Horses with MR showed more pronounced billowing of the mitral valve.Valve billowing was greater in horses in which the backward flow of blood increased towards the end of contraction of the heart. However, lower iMg levels were not related to the degree of valve billowing. In addition, the other three biomarkers studied (5-HT, NT-proBNP, and cTnI) did not show meaningful differences between horses with and without MR.

items.title: Deep learning optimisation for cardiology: Neural Architecture Search-driven arrhythmia classification with electrocardiograms.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for roughly 50% of all cardiac deaths. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is widely used for diagnosing cardiac disease. However, the complexity of interpretation limits the ECG's efficacy. Modern deep learning methods can assist clinicians in diagnosis. We applied Neural Architecture Search (NAS) to identify optimal deep learning architectures for classifying cardiac arrhythmias with ECGs. We applied the Differentiable Architecture Search strategy to an AutoFormer search and trained, validated, and tested the resulting model on the PhysioNet Challenge 2021 (PC21) dataset (n = 88,253 from three continents). We optimised hyperparameters on the NAS output, exploring input patch size, class weighting, and loss function. The PC21 metric and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) are the performance metrics. The NAS converged towards minimal architectural configurations (embedding dimension: 384, depth: 4, self-attention heads: 4, MLP ratio: 1) with a validation and test PC21 metric of 0.66 (PC21 winner: 0.63). The NAS-created network achieved an AUROC of 0.97 and a PC21 metric of 0.72 during testing (PC21 winner: 0.69). We tested the PC21 winner architecture (1D-convolutional neural network with attention mechanism) without the attention mechanism and with the NAS-suggested architecture of 4 self-attention heads (instead of 8). The architecture without the attention mechanism performed similarly to the one with 8 self-attention heads (AUROC: 0.90, PC21 metric: 0.69). The architecture with 4 self-attention heads scored an AUROC of 0.91 and improved the PC21 metric to 0.71. The attention mechanism visualisation for two SCD-related arrhythmias (premature ventricular contractions and prolonged QT-interval) showed more clinically relevant attention for the 4-self-attention-head architectures. We interpret architectural simplicity as driving performance in arrhythmia classification. The self-attention mechanism can autonomously abstract clinical representations, simplifying clinical deployment by eliminating the need for an explicit feature-extraction pipeline.

items.title: Ethnic disparities in outcomes of coronary artery bypass grafting in Israel.
items.abstract: Ethnic disparities after cardiac surgery are well reported. Israeli Arabs have lower life expectancy and greater frequency of cardiovascular risk factors. We sought to compare long-term outcomes following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) between Arab and Jewish patients in Israel. Retrospective study of adult patients with multivessel disease undergoing isolated CABG in three centers between January 1st, 2009, and December 31st, 2023. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). The cumulative incidence of MACCE was plotted using KM curves. The hazard ratio (HR) for Arabs vs. Jewish were calculated using multivariate Cox models. Our cohort included 6,330 patients, 1,819 (28.74%) and 4,511 (71.26%) patients were Arabs and Jewish, respectively. Median follow-up time was 78.32 months. Arab patients had higher rate of the primary outcome at median follow-up (46.26% vs 40.90%, HR 1.184, 95%CI: 1.09-1.286, P < 0.001) and there was no difference in mortality between the two groups (26.44% vs 26.45%, HR 1.004, 95%CI: 0.901-1.118, P = 0.82). After multivariable adjustment, the risk of MACCE was similar between the groups (adjusted HR 1.073, 95%CI: 0.965-1.193, P = 0.19). After multivariable adjustment for baseline and socioeconomic factors, ethnicity was not independently associated with worse long-term clinical outcomes in patients undergoing CABG in Israel, while unadjusted disparities remained evident.

items.title: Regulatory T Cell Interventions to Boost Anti-tumor Immune Responses.
items.abstract: FOXP3-expressing regulatory T cells (Tregs) are a specialized subset of T lymphocytes that are crucial for maintaining immune homeostasis and preventing autoimmunity. However, their pervasive presence and potent immunosuppressive functions within the tumor microenvironment (TME) are a barrier to anti-tumor immunity, presenting a major challenge for cancer immunotherapy. In this review, we discuss strategies for the therapeutic modulation of Tregs. Current and emerging promising technological approaches include antibody-based approaches, small molecule inhibitors, engineered Tregs, microbiome modulation, and Treg survival manipulations. Additionally, existing and promising combinatorial therapies integrate Treg cell targeting with complementary treatment strategies. The goal of this review is to spotlight how Treg-targeted interventions can overcome immune escape and ultimately enhance immunotherapy efficacy to improve clinical outcomes in cancer patients.

items.title: MultiMHC: a multiscale learning framework integrating sequence and residue contact topology for peptide-MHC binding prediction.
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of peptide-major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) binding is central to understanding antigen presentation and identifying T-cell epitopes in cancer immunotherapy. Although recent methods have achieved notable progress, most approaches rely predominantly on sequence-based features and only partially capture structural determinants of pMHC recognition. In this study, we present MultiMHC, a multiscale deep learning framework that integrates complementary sequential and biologically-informed residue contact topology for pMHC binding prediction. MultiMHC combines a recurrent neural network to model global sequence context with a graph-based representation to encode residue contact patterns derived from known pMHC binding interfaces. Features from these two pathways are subsequently fused to generate binding predictions across peptides of varying lengths. Benchmark evaluations show that MultiMHC achieves performance comparable to existing state-of-the-art methods, with particularly strong performance in ranking-based assessments. Moreover, evaluation on the Tumor Neoantigen Selection Alliance dataset showed that MultiMHC binding scores can enrich experimentally validated T-cell epitopes among top-ranked candidates, supporting its potential utility as an upstream binding-based filtering step in neoantigen discovery workflows. Together, these results highlight the value of incorporating residue interaction patterns and lightweight structural information into pMHC modeling and establish MultiMHC as a robust and extensive framework for antigen presentation analysis.

items.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Full Immunization Coverage among children aged 12-23 months in Kenya: A multi-level logistic regression analysis.
items.abstract: Full immunization coverage remains suboptimal in Kenya, despite the availability of effective vaccines. Understanding the multilevel factors influencing immunization uptake is essential for strengthening child health interventions. This study examines individual and community-level determinants of full immunization coverage among children aged 12-23 months in Kenya. To assess the individual and community-level factors associated with full immunization coverage among children aged from 12-23 months in Kenya using a multilevel analytical approach. A cross-sectional study was conducted using nationally representative survey data from Kenya. A two-level binary logistic regression model was used to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with full immunization coverage in Kenya. Adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported. The prevalence of full immunization coverage among children aged from 12-23 months in Kenya was 79.4% (95% CI: 78.13-81.25). A total of 3790 weighted children aged from 12-23 months were included. Children whose mothers were exposed to media (AOR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.01-1.34), delivered in health facilities (AOR = 2.88, 95% CI: 2.43-3.42), and attended antenatal care (AOR = 3.15, 95% CI: 2.10-4.73) had higher odds of full immunization. Children of average birth size (AOR = 1.68, 95% CI: 1.40-2.01) and those from rural areas (AOR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.22-1.69) were also more likely to be fully immunized. Higher maternal education showed a strong positive association: primary (AOR = 1.60), secondary (AOR = 2.14), and higher education (AOR = 1.74). Older maternal age increased immunization odds: 25-34 years (AOR = 1.49), 35-49 years (AOR = 2.15). Conversely, households with more than two under-five children (AOR = 0.72) and higher parity (2-5 children AOR = 0.78; 6 + AOR = 0.67) had lower odds. Community-level low maternal education also reduced the odds (AOR = 0.79). Maternal age, education, parity, media exposure, antenatal care, place of delivery, place of residence, and community education levels were associated with full immunization coverage in Kenya. Interventions should focus on improving maternal education, strengthening ANC services, promoting institutional deliveries, and enhancing outreach through media and community engagement.

items.title: RPL22 mutation is a favourable prognostic subset within mismatch repair-deficient endometrial cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Although mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) endometrial cancers are highly immunogenic and commonly responsive to immune checkpoint inhibitors, their heterogeneous outcomes indicate that dMMR status alone is insufficient to predict therapeutic benefit. The RPL22 gene - frequently mutated in microsatellite instability-high tumours - represents a candidate biomarker whose prognostic significance in dMMR endometrial cancer remains largely unexplored. In this retrospective cohort study, we analysed 250 patients with immunohistochemically confirmed dMMR endometrial cancer diagnosed between 2008 and 2022. The RPL22 p.K15Rfs*5 mutation was detected by Sanger sequencing and analysed in relation to MMR protein expression pattern, histologic subtype, treatment modality, recurrence pattern, cancer-specific survival (CSS), and progression-free survival (PFS). RPL22 mutations were identified in 78.4% (196/250) of dMMR tumours, at a comparable frequency in MLH1-PMS2-deficient (79.2%) and MSH2-MSH6-deficient (76.1%) cases ( p  = 0.596), and were unrelated to FIGO stage, treatment, or recurrence pattern. RPL22 -mutant tumours had significantly better CSS ( p   p  = 0.002) than wild-type tumours. MLH1-PMS2-deficient tumours showed worse CSS than MSH2-MSH6-deficient tumours ( p  = 0.008); within this subgroup, RPL22 -mutant tumours had better CSS and PFS than wild-type tumours ( p   p  = 0.005, respectively). In aggressive histologic subtypes, RPL22 mutations were associated with better CSS ( p  = 0.003). In multivariable analysis including FIGO stage, RPL22 mutations remained independently associated with better CSS (HR = 0.14; 95% CI, 0.05-0.43; p  = 0.001) and PFS (HR = 0.43; 95% CI, 0.23-0.81; p  = 0.009). In this hypothesis-generating retrospective cohort, the RPL22 p.K15Rfs*5 mutation identified a favourable prognostic subset within dMMR endometrial cancers, particularly among MLH1-PMS2-deficient tumours and aggressive histologic subtypes. Because treatment was not modelled and cancer-specific deaths were few, prospective validation in treatment-annotated cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation. Endometrial cancer, also known as cancer of the lining of the womb, is one of the most common cancers affecting women. In some of these tumours, the cellular machinery that normally corrects small mistakes in the DNA does not work – a feature that doctors describe as ‘mismatch repair deficiency’. Cancers with this feature often respond to modern treatments known as immunotherapies, but not all patients benefit in the same way, and doctors currently have no reliable way to predict who will do well and who will not.In this study, we asked whether a particular change in a gene called RPL22 could help identify patients whose cancer is likely to have a more favourable course. We examined tumour samples from 250 women with mismatch repair-deficient endometrial cancer treated at our hospital in Taiwan between 2008 and 2022, and we looked for a specific change in this gene.We found that women whose tumours carried the change were less likely to die of their cancer and less likely to see it return than women whose tumours did not carry the change. The favourable effect was especially clear in tumours that would otherwise be expected to behave more aggressively.These findings suggest that testing for this genetic change may one day help doctors identify women with a more favourable outlook. However, the results come from a single hospital, the treatments that patients received could not be fully taken into account, and the findings need to be confirmed in larger studies at other centres before the test can be used in routine clinical practice.
items.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology

items.title: Uncovering the immune microenvironmental atlas of breast cancer molecular subtypes based on single-cell transcriptomics.
items.abstract: Breast cancer progression is closely linked to immune cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME), but the immune landscape differences across HER2-positive (HER2+), triple-negative (TNBC), and ER-positive (ER+) subtypes have yet to be systematically characterized. In this study, we characterized immune landscape differences across HER2-positive (HER2+), triple-negative (TNBC), and ER-positive (ER+) breast cancers using single-cell RNA sequencing data, focusing on T cells, macrophages, and B cells. Our analysis revealed that cytotoxic CD8 + T cells were more abundant in TNBC but showed signs of dysfunction. Macrophage subsets, including an NDUFB8 + population, exhibited divergent functional orientations across subtypes. B cells in TNBC exhibited functional alterations, characterized by a decreased proportion of plasmablasts and an increased proportion of memory B cells. Single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering (SCENIC) analysis predicted a set of subtype-specific candidate transcription factors (TFs), including E2F8 across all subtypes and ATF7 in HER2 + tumors, whose activity correlated with clinical outcomes. Finally, mapping multicellular communication networks revealed both conserved and subtype-specific signaling pathways. Together, these results present a detailed transcriptional landscape of immune heterogeneity in breast cancer and contribute novel insights that may inform the design of subtype-specific immunotherapies.

items.title: Commonly expressed key driver genes in the pathogenesis of viral and non-viral liver cancer.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common and lethal liver cancer primarily associated with viral infections like hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV), as well as non-viral causes. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of these subtypes is essential for identifying potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In this study, an integrated bioinformatics approach was used to analyze publicly available datasets related to HBV-associated, HCV-associated, and non-viral HCC. Functional enrichment analyses and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed to identify key hub genes. Our analysis identified dysregulated genes across all HCC subtypes. Among these, GPC3 and SPARCL1 were significantly upregulated, while ALB and HNF4α were downregulated, and are involved in critical cancer pathways such as Wnt, PI3K/Akt, and p53 signaling. Functional analysis linked these DEGs to essential processes in tumorigenesis, including cell cycle regulation and immune modulation. Notably, SPARCL1 has been identified as a potential inhibitor of SPP1, a key driver of HCC. Validation using databases such as GEPIA and TNMplot confirmed the dysregulation of these genes in numerous HCC tissue samples and their significant association with patient prognosis. This study provides a comprehensive overview of HCC pathogenesis by suggesting a shared gene profile between viral and non-viral forms, paving the way for universal diagnostic markers and targeted therapies while highlighting the need for further experimental validation to advance precision medicine in HCC.

items.title: Bridging the birth dose gap: A scoping review of implementation challenges for birth dose and rotavirus vaccines in low- and middle-income countries.
items.abstract: Rotavirus vaccination (RVV) has substantially reduced childhood diarrhoeal morbidity and mortality globally. However, interest in neonatal or birth-dose schedules is increasing to provide earlier protection and potentially reduce intussusception risk. Understanding barriers and implementation challenges of current RVV and other birth-dose vaccines (BDVs), including hepatitis B birth dose, Bacillus Calmette-Guérin, and oral polio vaccine, is essential to inform this transition in low- and middle-income countries. This review therefore aims to examine the supply- and demand-side factors influencing the uptake, timeliness, and implementation of RVV and BDV in low- and middle-income countries. A scoping review was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, and grey literature from Portal Garuda from database inception to 5 March 2025. Original studies assessing determinants, enablers, and barriers of any BDV or RVV implementation, uptake, or timeliness were included. An analytical framework was developed inductively to classify factors as supply- or demand-side and was refined through discussions among reviewers. From 8,502 identified records, a total of 93 articles were included in the review. Identified supply-side enablers and barriers encompassed domains related to policy and governance, health system capacity, healthcare accessibility, and programmatic interventions. On the demand side, key enablers included higher caregiver education, higher socioeconomic status, health facility birth, and older maternal age, whereas major barriers included home birth, lower socioeconomic status, rural residence for BDV, and incomplete or delayed uptake of other routine vaccinations for RVV. Implementation and uptake of BDV and RVV were influenced by both supply- and demand-side factors, including policy support, health system capacity and access, targeted interventions, and socioeconomic disparities in vaccine uptake. Transitioning from infant-dose to birth-dose RVV will require addressing existing implementation challenges and ensuring timely vaccination at birth to achieve equitable coverage.

items.title: A Biologically Optimized PEG-IFN-α2 Variant Exhibits Potent Anti-HBV and Immunomodulatory Efficacy.
items.abstract: Human interferon-alpha (IFN-α) includes 13 subtypes, but only IFN-α2 (a/b) is clinically approved for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) therapy, limited by adverse effects and suboptimal response rates. Previously, we identified IFN-α14 as a superior anti-HBV subtype compared to IFN-α2, leading to the engineering of the IFN-α2-EIFK variant, which mimics IFN-α14's enhanced antiviral activity through targeted mutations at receptor-binding sites. However, the in vivo anti-HBV effects of IFN-α2-EIFK remained unexplored due to its short plasma half-life and lack of immunocompetent murine systems suitable for evaluating human IFN-α activity. Using an immunocompetent IFNAR-hEC mouse model and HBV-infected human-liver chimeric mice etc, we demonstrated that N-terminally PEGylated IFN-α2-EIFK (PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK) suppressed HBV replication and antigen expression approximately 10-fold more effectively than PEG-IFN-α2 at equivalent mass doses, while concurrently activating IFN-γ-like signaling pathways in both hepatocytes and immune cells. Subsequent single-cell analysis of intrahepatic immune cells from IFNAR-hEC mice showed that PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK was associated with enhanced antigen-presenting capacity of macrophages, dendritic cells (DCs), and B cells. In addition, PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK was found to preferentially promote M1-like macrophage polarization, and modulate PD-L1/PD-1 interactions between macrophages and CD8 + T cells, accompanied by attenuation of an exhaustion-associated CD8 + T cell state. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK exhibits greater anti-HBV activity and immunomodulatory potency than PEG-IFN-α2 under equivalent mass dosing, supporting its potential as an enhanced therapeutic candidate for CHB.

items.title: Diagnostic performance and clinical utility of an HCV antigen-antibody combination assay across diverse real-world cohorts.
items.abstract: The traditional two-step serological screening algorithm for hepatitis C virus (HCV) is frequently hindered by diagnostic delays, high molecular testing costs, and high false-positive rates due to non-specific serological interference. The Elecsys HCV Duo assay simultaneously detects HCV core antigen (Ag) and anti-HCV antibodies (Ab); however, comprehensive validation across highly heterogeneous clinical populations, particularly in highly vulnerable groups such as hemodialysis patients, remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world diagnostic and operational utility of the HCV Duo assay across diverse clinical cohorts. This multi-center study evaluated 1,844 patients stratified into hemodialysis ( n = 856), outpatient ( n = 477), inpatient ( n = 384), and health checkup ( n = 127) settings. Using HCV RNA as the reference standard, the dual-marker assay effectively eliminated 98.8% of low-reactivity (cutoff index [COI] 0.90-3.00) and 44.2% of moderate-reactivity (COI 3.01-10.00) conventional false positives. The Ag module achieved 66.51% overall sensitivity, 99.88% specificity, and a 98.58% positive predictive value. Notably, the assay maintained robust diagnostic reliability against uremia-induced interference in the hemodialysis cohort, where applying a Youden-optimized diagnostic threshold improved Ag sensitivity from 65.0% to 75.0%. Translating these performance metrics into a profile-driven triage strategy safely eliminated the need for routine RNA confirmatory testing in up to 33.3% of the simulated cohort, significantly reducing reliance on downstream molecular analysis.IMPORTANCEThe HCV Duo assay offers simultaneous antigen and antibody detection; however, laboratories lack robust evidence regarding its operational utility across highly diverse patient populations. Consequently, screening protocols remain reliant on delayed and costly RNA confirmation, particularly for complex groups like hemodialysis patients, where uremic interference frequently confounds standard serological testing. This study fills this gap by demonstrating the assay's robust diagnostic stability across four distinct clinical environments while specifically resolving the long-standing serological blind spot in the hemodialysis cohort. By providing evidence-based, cohort-specific insights and an actionable triage algorithm, this research enables laboratories to implement more efficient, tailored screening pathways. These advances significantly reduce the reliance on unnecessary molecular testing, accelerate clinical decision-making, and provide a pragmatic framework to support global HCV elimination mandates.

items.title: Mitochondrial Oxysterol Signaling in Epigenetic Regulation and Therapeutic Development.
items.abstract: Oxysterols are oxygenated cholesterol derivatives with receptor-dependent and epigenetic activities. This review examines how mitochondrial cholesterol metabolism and oxysterol sulfation may connect lipid metabolism to DNA methylation and communication between hepatocytes and macrophages. Biochemical studies show that 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC) and 27-hydroxycholesterol (27HC) activate DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), whereas their 3-sulfated derivatives inhibit the activities of DNMT1, DNMT3A, and DNMT3B. Cholestenoic acid (CA) has a concentration-dependent effect, activating DNMT1 at lower concentrations and inhibiting it at higher concentrations. In hepatocyte models, these activities are associated with altered promoter CpG methylation and expression of genes involved in lipid metabolism, inflammatory responses, and cell survival. The sulfated CA metabolite, 3β-sulfate-5-cholestenoic acid (3SCA), is secreted by hepatocytes and modifies inflammatory gene expression in macrophages. We propose an oxysterol epigenetic rheostat in which metabolite concentrations and sulfation influence DNMT activities. Published animal studies support protective effects of 25-hydroxycholesterol 3-sulfate in fatty liver disease, endotoxemia, and acetaminophen-induced liver injury. Its clinical formulation, larsucosterol, has shown favorable hepatic and metabolic signals in Phase 1b fatty liver studies and nominally significant mortality reductions in prespecified US Phase 2b alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) analyses. These encouraging findings require confirmation because the overall Phase 2b primary endpoint was not met. Larsucosterol has received Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for AH and is currently being evaluated in a registrational Phase 3 trial.

items.title: An Ecological Analysis of Rising Gastrointestinal Cancer Burden in Low- and Middle-Income Countries From 1990 to 2023.
items.abstract: IntroductionGastrointestinal cancers (GICs) impose substantial health loss in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). We examined long-term burden patterns and temporal changes from 1990 to 2023.MethodsThis ecological secondary analysis used Global Burden of Disease 2023 estimates of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and age-standardised DALY rates (ASDRs) for six GIC types in 130 LMICs from 1990 to 2023. Joinpoint regression described temporal trends, and decomposition analysis separated population growth, population aging, and changes in age-specific DALY rates.ResultsFrom 1990 to 2023, total GIC-related DALYs increased from 34.72 to 43.16 million in upper-middle-income countries (UMCs), from 7.20 to 19.76 million in lower-middle-income countries (LMCs), and from 1.88 to 4.69 million in low-income countries (LCs). In UMCs, ASDRs for all GICs except pancreatic cancer declined, especially for esophageal and stomach cancers. In LMCs and LCs, ASDRs for stomach and liver cancers declined, whereas the other four subtypes increased. The shares of global DALYs occurring in UMCs increased for colorectal and pancreatic cancers but decreased for stomach and liver cancers. In contrast, DALYs rose for all six subtypes in LMCs and LCs. Decomposition analysis indicated that population growth and aging were important demographic contributors to the increase in DALYs, whereas the epidemiological changes was negative in UMCs and counterbalanced part of the demographic contribution.ConclusionThe overall DALY burden of GICs increased across LMICs, whereas ASDR trends were heterogeneous across cancer subtypes. These findings support country- and cancer-specific prevention and care priorities.

items.title: Robotic transabdominal specimen extraction vs. transanal specimen extraction for sigmoid and upper rectal cancer: a comparative analysis of short-term outcomes.
items.abstract: Robotic surgery has become an established approach for the management of patients with sigmoid colon and upper rectal cancer (SURC). Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES), which avoids an additional abdominal wall incision, is a widely used minimally invasive approach in colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. It remains uncertain whether transanal specimen extraction, classified as type IV natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES-IV), offers advantages over conventional transabdominal specimen extraction (TASE) during robot-assisted surgery for SURC. We retrospectively compared the perioperative outcomes of the two extraction strategies. We retrospectively reviewed 254 patients who underwent robot-assisted surgery for SURC at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University, between January 2019 and January 2026. Ninety-one patients received NOSES-IV, and 163 received TASE. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 83 patients per group were included, and their short-term perioperative outcomes were compared. After matching, the baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between the two groups. Compared with the TASE group, the NOSES-IV group had a shorter gastrointestinal reconstruction time (P < 0.001) and less intraoperative blood loss (P = 0.022). Patients in the NOSES-IV group also ambulated (P = 0.029), passed flatus (P = 0.018), and resumed semiliquid diet earlier (P = 0.038). On postoperative days 1, 3 and 5, their C-reactive protein levels were lower (P = 0.017). They also had fewer incision-related complications (P = 0.014), a shorter postoperative hospital stay (P = 0.034), and lower visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores (P = 0.008). In this retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort, compared with TASE, robot-assisted NOSES-IV for SURC was associated with fewer incision-related complications, less postoperative pain, and earlier recovery. The total operative time, lymph node yield, resection margin status, and anorectal function at 3 months did not differ between the groups. These findings suggest that NOSES-IV is a feasible option for appropriately selected patients, but confirmation in larger, multicentre, prospective studies with longer follow-up is needed.

items.title: CircIKBKB promotes hepatocellular carcinoma stemness and EMT via TAF15-PTCH1-mediated Hedgehog activation.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Accumulating studies in recent years have confirmed that circular RNAs (circRNAs) are involved in the regulation of tumor initiation and progression. Nevertheless, the precise functions and underlying molecular mechanisms of circRNAs in HCC remain to be thoroughly investigated. In this study, we identified a circular RNA derived from the IKBKB gene, designated circIKBKB (database accession number: hsa_circ_0084102), which exhibits significantly elevated expression in HCC cell lines. Functional experiments demonstrated that circIKBKB promotes HCC cell proliferation, sustains cancer stemness properties, and induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Mechanistically, circIKBKB directly interacts with the RNA-binding protein TATA-box binding protein associated factor 15 (TAF15) and suppresses its polyubiquitination-mediated proteasomal degradation, thereby maintaining intracellular TAF15 protein stability. The upregulated TAF15 further binds to Patched 1 (PTCH1) mRNA and enhances its transcript stability, which consequently drives aberrant activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway. Both in vitro and in vivo validation assays confirmed that overexpression of PTCH1 partially reversed the phenotypic effects induced by circIKBKB knockdown. Collectively, our findings uncover the regulatory mechanism of circIKBKB in mediating aberrant activation of the Hedgehog pathway in HCC, and this work may provide a potential interventional strategy for HCC treatment.

items.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic targets in HCC. Computational ADMET screening indicated SP possesses favourable drug-likeness, high oral bioavailability, and low toxicity. Molecular docking and 500-ns molecular dynamics simulations showed stable SP binding to HDAC2, with ligand RMSD of 1.5-2.0 Å, protein RMSD of 3.0-4.5 Å, and active-site RMSF < 1.0 Å, supported by persistent Zn²⁺ coordination and hydrophobic interactions. In vitro evaluations in HepG2 cells revealed distinct dose-dependent cytotoxicity (IC₅₀ = 8.2 mM) and pronounced morphological alterations. Furthermore, SP treatment strongly downregulated the mRNA expression of HDAC2 (0.31-fold, p < 0.001) and HDAC6 (0.60-fold, p < 0.05). This suppression was accompanied by a significant, dose-dependent increase in caspase-3/7 activity, confirming apoptotic induction. These findings suggest SP functions as a dual-action epigenetic modulator in HCC, promoting apoptosis by downregulating HDAC2/6 expression and potentially inhibiting their enzymatic activity. However, biochemical assays, protein-level validation, and in vivo HCC models are necessary to validate this inhibition.
